tweet_summary: Tweet presents a video of a teacher slapping a student as a real classroom altercation and asks viewers whether the teacher was right to hit her back.
why_note_decision: The video is a scripted skit produced by social-media creator Kenyon W (KenyonWShow), who routinely produces dramatized teacher-student conflict scenes. The tweet presents it as a real incident inviting moral judgement, so a context note is warranted. One commenter ('This woman does tons of skits. This is fake.') and many engaged users believing it is real confirm the misleading framing.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note (1) states the video is a scripted/staged skit, not a real classroom incident, (2) attributes it to creator Kenyon W (KenyonWShow / @kinyawn) or links to the original skit upload, and (3) provides at least one source (Facebook KenyonWShow page, TikTok @kinyawn, or equivalent). FAIL if the note treats the incident as real, debates whether striking was justified, or only says 'unverified' without identifying it as a known scripted creator's skit.
reference_note: This video is a scripted skit produced by creator Kenyon W (KenyonWShow / @kinyawn on TikTok), not a real classroom incident. https://www.facebook.com/KenyonWShow/videos/student-slaps-teacher-then-immediately-gets-taught-a-lesson/991053859064934/

fact_check.notes: Kenyon W (Wellington) runs a known channel producing classroom conflict skits. Multiple uploads in this exact format with the same actors confirm staging.

importance.lens_rationale: 586K views and inflammatory race/gender framing ('young white female ... slapped him'); correcting staged-content-as-news erodes a common engagement-farming pattern.
